package_organization.issue_character: The problems are structural and systemic: the two most central packages in the codebase (base/models/ at 59 files and base/services/ at 40 files) are severely overloaded flat directories mixing unrelated domain concerns, and the base/ parent directory itself is a 30-file catch-all; these are not isolated outliers but the load-bearing center of the project.
package_organization.score_rationale: The codebase sits well below the 60-threshold anchor ('organization regularly obscures ownership; a developer must search rather than navigate'): a developer looking for video-infrastructure models (BBB, Janus, Turn, Streaming, World) has to scan through 59 sibling files to find them because they share the flat base/models/ directory with ticketing, CFP, and messaging models. The app-level separation (agenda/, cfp/, control/) is genuinely good and pushes the score above 40, but the central base/ subsystem — which is the most-imported part of the codebase — is a navigation obstacle at every layer (models, services, and the base directory itself). The score is 52 because the per-app structure is readable but the core shared layer, which every developer touches, requires searching rather than navigation.

issues.suggestion: Stage the reorganization in four steps: (1) Create subdirectories base/models/video/ (bbb.py, janus.py, turn.py, streaming.py, stream_schedule.py, room.py, roomquestion.py, roulette.py, poll.py, poster.py, world.py), base/models/ticketing/ (orders.py, checkin.py, seating.py, invoices.py, giftcards.py, vouchers.py, billing.py, product.py, tax.py, waitinglist.py, cart implied via orders), base/models/cfp/ (cfp.py, review.py, submission.py, track.py, type.py, slot.py, schedule.py, question.py, resource.py, feedback.py), base/models/messaging/ (chat.py, mail.py, notifications.py, announcement.py). (2) Move files with `git mv`, update internal relative imports within each cluster. (3) Update base/models/__init__.py to import from subpackages (e.g., `from .video import BBBServer, JanusServer, Room`). (4) Validate with `python manage.py check --deploy` and run the test suite to catch broken imports. world.py should additionally be moved to eventyay_common/models/ since it is only referenced from eventyay_common/.

stripe_utils.py (payment provider integration), reportlab.py (PDF rendering library wrapper), and plugin_enable.py (plugin lifecycle) do not share concern with date/time helpers or JSON utilities — 'helpers' is a catch-all with no coherent ownership criterion
helpers/ is imported by base/exporters/ 4 times and base/ 2 times — it serves multiple distinct consumers with unrelated needs
issues.suggestion: Rename 'helpers' to domain-specific subpackages: extract payment-adjacent code (stripe_utils.py) to eventyay/payments/utils.py near the payment plugin; move reportlab.py to base/rendering/reportlab.py alongside invoice.py and pdf.py; move plugin_enable.py to common/plugins.py. Rename the remainder to eventyay/utils/ to signal it is a utilities package rather than a generic dumping ground. Run `grep -r 'from eventyay.helpers' app/` to enumerate all callers before renaming, then update paths and run `python manage.py check`.

root_causes: The project grew by accumulating models and services into the base/ mega-package without enforcing domain boundaries as new features (video rooms, BBB, Janus, polls, posters, roulette) were added alongside the original ticketing domain — the flat structure is a historical accumulation artifact

The absence of a 'module owns its models' convention (as seen in cfp/, schedule/) for the video and live-event subsystems caused video-domain models (World, Room, BBB, Janus) to land in the ticketing-focused base/models/ instead of a domain-scoped package
The helpers/ package acts as a permanent staging area for code that has no obvious home — contributing to a structurally undifferentiated utility surface
